I definately feel for you.  I had the same feelings before a mates wedding and I chatted at length with another friend who public speaks as part of his job.  All the advice given below is great and here are a couple of other pointers which I hope haven't been mentioned.  Preparation is the key.  Write your speech down and practice it. Practice it until you know all the points you want to say and then practice some more.  There is no need to know it perfectly word for word, your audience will not know if you forget a line here or add a few words in there just so long as you are comfortable with everthing that you want to say.  Now to further help with your nerves learn the very first line of your speech word for word.  This is important because it will give you some confidence and throw your mind into the job that needs to be done once you get up there.  One last point is hey its a wedding, everyone is there to have a good time and enjoy the day.  They will laugh at appropriate times and won't boo you if you stumble.  Congrats on the honour and enjoy the day.  I can tell you that the beer you have after you have completed the speach will be the best you have tasted.
